change: One change against powered_split_20261001: search_code context cap 1,500 -> 1,000 tokens (read_code unchanged; catalog differs only in that number). Reverted after this study: production source is again identical to the powered-study candidate.
offline_prediction: Replay of the powered study (168 recorded searches, byte-exact) predicted 0.80x native tokens and ~81/100 supported, holding the model actions fixed.
design: Same 100 previously queried questions, three fresh arms, gpt-6-luna, six-call stop, no retries; reserved unseen-20260929-* never loaded. Launched detached; no interruption.
mechanism: The model compensated for smaller searches with more calls (303 vs 267; one-call runs 21 -> 12, six-call runs 7 -> 11). Runs cost ~4k tokens when the first search already holds all graded evidence and ~13k when it holds under half; the smaller cap made complete first searches rarer (first-query replay: 1,000 -> 39/200, 1,500 -> 60/200).
replication: Native scored 69 then 80 on the same questions and code (run-to-run spread ~11 points). Split scored 85 then 87 and cost 0.970x then 1.026x native tokens; versus the control it was 0.862x and 0.833x.
next_option_offline: Capping only the split reader at 4 calls is estimated at 8,347 tokens on the powered run (0.846x that run native) with complete-evidence status unchanged in 99/100 runs; this breaks the equal-stop rule of the gate and was not run.
limitations: Arm-blind coding-assistant review; 15 of 20 first-wave reviewers were cut off by usage limits and their groups re-run in waves; all 300 reviews passed integrity checks.
